newsitem.title: USA: IMF gold sale proposal runs into problems -sources.
newsitem.headline: IMF gold sale proposal runs into problems -sources.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is running into big problems reaching agreement on a controversial proposal to sell off some of its gold to aid the world's poor, international monetary sources said on Monday.
The sources, who declined to be named, said that IMF board members look unlikely to be able to settle their differences on the plan when they resume talks on Wednesday.
"I don't see an agreement on Wednesday," one source said.

IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, has proposed selling five million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.
But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- have opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.

The IMF board spent much of Friday discussing ways to help the world's poorest nations. A number of sources said that no consensus in favor of the gold sales plan emerged during the initial discussions.
